newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly steady despite crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly steady despite crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Wednesday in thin trade, with supply and demand fairly well-balanced though buyers backed away as crude crumbled, industry sources said.
"Fundamentally, the market is in balance, but when crude falls, buyers get more cautious," said one cash trader, adding mild East Coast weather this week has curbed utility demand.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at $15.75-16.00. July one percent paper sold between $15.45-60, down slightly with softer crude, while August was talked at $15.35-60 and September at $15.35-50, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again gained slightly to about the $17 area on some limited buying interest for two New England utilities.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to down slightly, with 2.2 percent now quoted at $14.30-55, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with three percent still at $14.50 and one percent at $16.00.

New York city gate gas prices gained a couple of cents Wednesday to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a similar amount to about $2.22/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
